findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key you were issued. Append it as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Query parameter api_key returns 401 with detail: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. Key must be supplied in HTTP header 'X-API-Key'.
findings.how_found: Probed endpoints with query param and observed 401 response instructing header usage.
findings.impact: All frontend requests fail immediately if using the documented query param authentication.

findings.documented: expires_in: 86400 (24 hours). Tokens are valid for 24 hours with no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Tokens expire in 900 seconds (15 minutes). Response includes refresh_token and refresh_url: '/auth/refresh'.
findings.how_found: Inspected JSON response from POST /auth/login with demo user credentials.
findings.impact: Sessions terminate after 15 minutes unless the client periodically exchanges the refresh token at /auth/refresh.

findings.documented: Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: The /health endpoint returns server_time and reference_date carrying an explicit +05:30 Asia/Kolkata timezone offset rather than a UTC 'Z' suffix.
findings.impact: Clients and schema parsers expecting strict UTC strings ending in 'Z' fail validation or calculate offsets incorrectly.

findings.documented: Collection endpoints take 'page' (1-indexed) and 'limit' (default 20, max 200), returning { total, page, page_size, results }.
findings.actual: Endpoints use offset-based pagination returning { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results } where page and page_size are undefined. Server default limit is 50.
findings.how_found: Inspected response envelope keys across pagination requests.
findings.impact: Frontends using page numbers will continuously request offset 0 or fail to paginate properly.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Returns inactive listings. Each listing includes an undocumented 'is_live' boolean flag that must be filtered client-side.
findings.how_found: Observed listings with is_live: false in the retrievable dataset.
findings.impact: Users will be shown withdrawn/expired listings if the UI relies on server-side filtering.

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Listings sourced from 'magichomes' provide carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square meters (e.g. 70-150 sqm for 2-4 BHK units) rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Examined distribution of carpet_area and price/sqft across websites; magichomes records have ~10x higher price/area ratio due to square meter units.
findings.impact: Displays absurdly small room areas (e.g. 80 sqft for a 2BHK) and inflates calculated price-per-square-foot by 10.76x.

findings.documented: Money: Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API. price_min and price_max are in rupees.
findings.actual: Projects report price_min and price_max in floating-point Crores (for values < 15, e.g. 1.66 - 5.83 Cr) and Lakhs (for values >= 15, e.g. 55.8 - 98.9 L), not integer rupees.
findings.how_found: Analyzed price_min and price_max on /v1/projects; all 400 records have values < 1000.
findings.impact: Projects display prices as ₹2 to ₹98 instead of Crores/Lakhs, breaking sorting and budget filtering.

findings.documented: Listing records represent genuine properties with valid structural attributes.
findings.actual: 123 records contain physically impossible values: negative prices (e.g. -8,550,000), floor greater than total_floors (e.g. floor 26 in an 11-floor tower), or carpet_area greater than super_built_up_area.
findings.how_found: Ran automated invariant assertions across all listings.
findings.impact: Displays nonsensical and negative values to end users and crashes layout assumptions.

findings.documented: Active sale listings represent valid properties for sale.
findings.actual: 6 listings contain monthly rental rates entered into the sale price field (ranging from ₹5,030 to ₹26,260) designed as lead-generation bait.
findings.how_found: Queried listings with price < 100,000 and matched amounts to typical monthly rent brackets.
findings.impact: Distorts median property sale prices and misleads homebuyers with fake sub-₹30k purchase listings.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: For 298 out of 400 projects, the reported total_listings count differs from the actual count of listings associated with that project_id.
findings.how_found: Aggregated listing count by project_id and compared against each project's total_listings property.
findings.impact: Project overview badges display inaccurate inventory counts compared to actual available units.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city.
findings.impact: Dashboard relying on server-side summary fails; aggregates must be computed client-side.

findings.documented: the endpoint accepts a limit parameter to control the number of records returned per request
findings.actual: the server respects the requested limit when it is within the allowed range, but caps larger requests at a maximum limit of 50
findings.how_found: requested limit=20 and received limit=20 with count=20; a separate request with limit=100 returned limit=50 and count=50
findings.impact: none - callers requesting more than 50 records must paginate, but the endpoint still exposes has_more and offset for retrieving subsequent records

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching the filters, and clients can use total to determine how many pages to request
findings.actual: The API reports total=382, but pagination exposes 400 unique project records before has_more becomes false
findings.how_found: Paginated through /v1/projects with limit=50 until has_more=false. The final response had offset=350, count=50, producing 400 records. All 400 project_id values were verified to be unique.
findings.impact: Clients relying on total to determine the number of pages may stop after retrieving 382 records and miss 18 valid project records.

findings.documented: Favourites endpoints are documented at /v1/favourites: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body {"id": "..."}, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found. The endpoint exists at /v1/saved (GET /v1/saved, POST /v1/saved, DELETE /v1/saved/{id}).
findings.how_found: Probed GET /v1/favourites which returned 404; probed alternative resource names and confirmed /v1/saved returns 200 with { count, results }.
findings.impact: Any frontend adhering to the documented /v1/favourites route fails to fetch or save listings; all user bookmarking features break with 404 errors.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings — same locality, same bedroom count, price within 15%.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found. Probing /v1/listings with query parameters like ?similar_to={id} returns 200 OK but quietly ignores the parameter and serves the default unfiltered catalog (including the target property itself).
findings.how_found: Sent GET request to /v1/listings/MAG-6002450/similar which returned 404; compared results of /v1/listings?similar_to=MAG-6002450 against bare /v1/listings and found identical record IDs in identical order.
findings.impact: Detail pages cannot retrieve server-computed comparable listings; recommendation logic must be implemented client-side by querying /v1/listings filtered by locality and BHK.
